chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, with his chain of narrators, that he ascribed it (to the Prophet), saying:
The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: The best of eid [1] is blood-letting – meaning habit [2] – it clears vision and repels disease.

key_terms.الْعِيد: eid (festival/occasion), here interpreted as a recurring habit or custom

ai.seo_question: What is the prophetic benefit of regular blood-letting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith elevates *hijamah* (cupping) to the status of the 'best Eid' by interpreting the term as a recurring beneficial habit rather than a singular festival. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) highlights its dual therapeutic value in clarifying vision and expelling disease, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating physical health with spiritual well-being. This narration underscores the prophetic tradition of preventive medicine as a form of gratitude and self-care.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, with his chain of narrators, that he ascribed it, saying:
The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: The best of eid [1] is blood-letting – meaning habit [2] – it clears vision and repels disease.
